transcript: An entire country went to sleep Thursday [short pause] and woke up Saturday. This is Samoa, December twenty eleven. Friday the thirtieth never happened here. No storm. No glitch. It was a law, passed on purpose. Samoa sat just east of the International Date Line, the invisible seam where each new day begins. Its biggest trading partners, Australia and New Zealand, sat just across it, almost a full day ahead. So your Friday was their Saturday. Your Sunday was their Monday. Like, two working days lost, every week. The fix was simple. At midnight on Thursday the twenty-ninth, Samoa moved to the other side of the line and landed on Saturday the thirty-first. Here's the twist. [short pause] Samoa had already done this once, backwards. In eighteen ninety-two, to match American traders, it lived through the same day twice. Two Fourth of Julys. So after a hundred and nineteen years, the country finally returned the extra day. Nobody noticed. [deadpan] Everyone was asleep.
